# Overview

## What this deck shows

The ATF2 paper (Gómez-Deza et al., *Neuron* 2026) defines one pro-apoptotic cascade:

**DLK / LZK (MAP3K12/13) → MKK4/7 (MAP2K4/7) → JNK (MAPK8/9/10) → phospho-ATF2 → JUN → CASP3 / PUMA / BIM / HRK**

For each dataset below, the slides give the **gene detected** (rat symbols), its **line in the original source file**, and the **fold change / ratio + p-value**.

Every table is backed by a small CSV that was extracted from the raw data, so the rows can be searched directly. The `grep` reference commands on the last slides point at those extracted CSVs.

## Source files and the extracted CSVs

| Dataset | Original source file | Extracted CSV (searchable) |
|---|---|---|
| Newly synthesized (nascent axonal) | `IPA/Axons_table_proteins.csv` | `ATF2_analysis/nascent_ATF2_hits.csv` |
| Total proteome | `IPA/GeneSymbol_Table.csv` | `ATF2_analysis/total_proteome_ATF2_hits.csv` |
| Phosphoproteomics | `IPA/Phosphoproteomics data for PP2Ci_16April2026.xlsx` (Excel only) | `ATF2_analysis/phospho_ATF2_hits.csv` |

The first column of every extracted CSV (`source_line` / `source_row`) is the row number in the original file.

# Newly synthesized (nascent axonal) proteome

## proNGF vs Ctrl

Source: `IPA/Axons_table_proteins.csv` — Extracted: `nascent_ATF2_hits.csv`

| Src line | Gene (role) | Unique pep | Cov % | proNGF/Ctrl | T-test (p) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 967 | Casp3 (Caspase-3) | 1 | 2.89 | 0.90 | 0.46 |

**Only Casp3 is detected** (single peptide, low coverage → weak ID), and it does not change with proNGF.
None of ATF2, DLK, LZK, JNKs, MKK4/7, JUN, ATF3/4, FOS, CHOP, PUMA, BIM, HRK were detected.

## Total proteome — notes

- **Robustly identified** (≥3 peptides): Mapk9, Map2k7, Casp3, Map2k4, Mapk8.
- **Weak ID** (1 peptide): Fos, Map3k13 (LZK).
- **Not detected:** ATF2, DLK (Map3k12), c-Jun (Jun), Mapk10/JNK3, ATF3, ATF4, CHOP, CEBPG, PUMA, BIM, HRK, γH2AX.
- **No significant treatment effect** in the proNGF or proNGF+BDNF arms (all p > 0.05); only weak upward trends for Casp3 and Fos in proNGF+BDNF (p ≈ 0.06–0.07).
- Abundances are TMT-normalized (~100/channel), so identification is judged by peptide count / coverage, not raw value.

# Phosphoproteomics (nerve-crush model)

## ⚠ Different experiment

`Phosphoproteomics data for PP2Ci_16April2026.xlsx` is **not** the proNGF/BDNF study.
It is a **sciatic-nerve-crush** dataset: **Naïve vs Crushed**, with crushed arms treated by DMSO / CK2 inhibitor / PP2C inhibitor.
The column shown is **log2(Crushed / Naïve)** with its p-value. (−log10P ≥ 1.30 ⇒ p ≤ 0.05.)

## Significant phosphosites (p ≤ 0.05)

Source: Excel → Extracted: `phospho_ATF2_hits.csv`

| Excel row | Gene (role) | Phosphosite | log2(Crush/Naïve) | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1807  | Map3k12 (DLK)  | pThr43/45 | **+0.47** | **0.0001** |
| 17647 | Jund (JunD)    | pSer245/249 | −0.48 | 0.031 |
| 2417  | Casp3 (Casp-3) | pSer26/29 | +0.39 | 0.043 |
| 1506  | Map3k12 (DLK)  | pThr9/11/13 | +0.52 | 0.045 |
| 5441  | Map2k4 (MKK4)  | pSer255 | +0.18 | 0.047 |
| 15960 | Map2k4 (MKK4)  | pSer88 | −0.30 | 0.049 |

**Headline:** the apical kinase **DLK (Map3k12) is significantly more phosphorylated after injury (pThr43/45, ~1.4×, p ≈ 1×10⁻⁴)** — consistent with the paper placing DLK at the top of the cascade.

## Non-significant phosphosites (p > 0.05)

| Excel row | Gene (role) | Phosphosite | log2(Crush/Naïve) | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1055  | Jund (JunD)   | pSer100 | +0.61 | 0.104 |
| 1996  | Junb (JunB)   | pThr117 | +0.45 | 0.126 |
| 3769  | Map3k12 (DLK) | pSer569 | +0.28 | 0.129 |
| 3871  | Map2k4 (MKK4) | pSer88  | +0.27 | 0.057 |
| 4108  | Jund (JunD)   | pSer245/249 | +0.26 | 0.061 |
| 6925  | Map2k4 (MKK4) | pThr78  | +0.11 | 0.211 |
| 8724  | Map2k4 (MKK4) | pSer88  | +0.04 | 0.826 |
| 10501 | **Atf2 (core driver)** | **pSer94** (non-activating S-P site) | −0.04 | 0.668 |
| 14598 | Map2k4 (MKK4) | pSer391/392 | −0.21 | 0.385 |
| 18052 | Map2k4 (MKK4) | pSer88  | −0.57 | 0.086 |

**ATF2 caveat:** detected, but only at pSer94 (not the JNK/p38 activation-loop Thr69/71), low coverage, and unchanged by injury. c-Jun, JNKs, MKK7, ATF3/4, CHOP, FOS phosphosites were not captured.

# Find the lines yourself (grep reference)

## How to look up a gene in the extracted CSVs

These are **reference commands only** — copy one into a terminal (WSL / Linux / macOS) if you want to locate a gene's row yourself. `grep -n` prints the line number; the `source_line` / `source_row` column in each row gives the position in the original file.

Newly synthesized:

```
grep -n -i "Casp3" ATF2_analysis/nascent_ATF2_hits.csv
```

Total proteome (any pathway gene):

```
grep -n -i -E "Fos|Mapk9|Map2k7|Casp3|Map2k4|Mapk8|Map3k13" ATF2_analysis/total_proteome_ATF2_hits.csv
```

## Grep reference — phospho CSV

Phosphoproteomics (extracted from the Excel file):

```
grep -n -i -E "Atf2|Map3k12|Map2k4|Junb|Jund|Casp3" ATF2_analysis/phospho_ATF2_hits.csv
```

Just DLK and ATF2:

```
grep -n -i -E "Map3k12|Atf2" ATF2_analysis/phospho_ATF2_hits.csv
```

To search the **original** (non-extracted) CSVs instead, point the same pattern at `IPA/Axons_table_proteins.csv` or `IPA/GeneSymbol_Table.csv`.
